newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: West resumes satellite transmission from Albania.
newsitem.headline: West resumes satellite transmission from Albania.

text.p: Western television broadcasts resumed from Albania on Tuesday after Tirana gave in to criticism of its sweeping curbs on press freedom, a senior official of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) said.

The halt to EBU's television feeds, which lasted 24 hours, affected broadcasts by 25 Western companies and channels including Reuters Television, British Broadcasting Corporation, CNN, German networks ARD and ZDF, Italian RAI and French TF1.

It was the first such suspension of EBU's links since 1989, when China interrupted Western images of the military crackdown at Tiananmen Square, according to Tony Naets, head of EBU's Eurovision News Services.
Albania pulled the plug on Western television broadcasts out of the poor Balkan country on Monday as a nationwide state of emergency went into effect after weekend violence in the south.
Naets said the independent Geneva-based organisation had restarted transmission after receiving the go-ahead from Albania's PTT.
"We have just told by Albanian authorities that we can immediately resume satellite operations from Tirana," he told Reuters. "We have in fact started transmission again."
"I am looking at pictures from Tirana right now," he added.
Asked about the reversal, Naets, said: "To me, they (Albanian authorities) have given in to the pressure regarding the curbs on press freedom.
"They don't want to upset the West that much," he added.
"Twenty-five broadcasters were shut out last night. I am sure they all went to their embassies in Tirana to complain."
On Monday, Naets said the suspension of EBU's license effectively prevented the most visible way of reporting conditions in Albania.

The government declared a state of emergency and introduced a nationwide curfew and other emergency measures including media controls after two months of unrest following the collapse of dubious investment schemes climaxed at the weekend.
At least 12 people were reported killed, either in clashes or by stray bullets, as demonstrators in several southern towns raided weapons' depots and went on a rampage.

In Tirana on Tuesday, responding to an international outcry over media restrictions, Albanian justice ministry spokesman Agim Neza said the curbs did not apply to foreign news organisations. "You are free to report," Neza told Reuters.
President Sali Berisha was elected by parliament to a second five-year term in office on Monday.
In a televised address the day before, Berisha blamed foreign intelligence services and the former communist elite for the armed unrest in the south.
